patterns.platform: Shopify Dawn / Debut — sale badges and disabled/sold-out states
patterns.name: Insufficient contrast on sale badges and disabled buttons
patterns.description: 'Sale' / 'Sold out' badges and disabled 'Add to cart' buttons use light or theme-accent colors (e.g. light pink on white, grey-on-grey) that fall below 4.5:1 for the text, and the badge's non-text boundary can fall below 3:1. Common in default and lightly-customized Dawn/Debut palettes.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: This is largely auto-detectable: axe/Lighthouse compute text contrast ratios and flag <4.5:1. Edge cases tools may miss are disabled-control text (some scanners skip disabled elements) and badge text over gradient/image backgrounds, but the core is a measurable ratio, so humanJudgmentNeeded is false.
patterns.realWorldNote: Dawn audits specifically flag 'color contrast failures on sale badges and disabled elements' and multiple elements failing AA contrast. https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-dawn-theme-accessibility

patterns.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce themes — focus styling removed on interactive controls
patterns.name: Focus outline suppressed on swatches, buttons and links
patterns.description: Themes (or merchant CSS tweaks) apply outline:none / :focus{outline:0} to buttons, variant swatch labels, and links to 'clean up' the design, leaving no visible focus indicator. Keyboard users cannot tell which swatch/button is focused while navigating the product form.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Partly auto-detectable — some tools flag outline:none in CSS — but they cannot reliably confirm there is no adequate replacement indicator (a box-shadow or border swap may suffice) without observing the focused state. Reliable confirmation is by tabbing and watching; still, the core 'no visible focus' is verifiable, so flagged humanJudgmentNeeded=false with the caveat that replacement-indicator adequacy may need a look.
patterns.realWorldNote: Dawn/Shopify keyboard audits repeatedly cite suppressed/weak focus indicators; TestParty and Shopify theme best-practices emphasize visible focus on all interactive controls. https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-checkout-keyboard-navigation-fixes

patterns.platform: Tailwind CSS / Tailwind UI utility classes
patterns.name: focus:outline-none with no replacement focus ring
patterns.description: Developers apply Tailwind's focus:outline-none (often to kill the default blue ring on inputs/buttons) but never add a focus-visible:ring/outline replacement. Keyboard users get no visible focus indicator as they tab through forms and menus, making the UI unusable without a mouse.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
<button class="focus:outline-none px-4 py-2 bg-blue-600 text-white">
  Save
</button>
<!-- on Tab focus, nothing visible changes -->
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe/Lighthouse do not evaluate whether a visible focus indicator appears on :focus — there is no reliable automated check for 2.4.7. Detecting the missing ring requires actually tabbing and visually observing each control's focus state, i.e. human or pixel-diff judgment, especially since outline-none renders a transparent (not removed) outline.
patterns.realWorldNote: Tailwind's own docs warn that outline-none must be paired with an accessible focus state and recommend focus-visible: utilities; community guidance repeatedly flags focus:outline-none misuse. https://tailwindcss.com/docs/outline-style

patterns.platform: Bootstrap default theme (buttons, alerts, form-validation, placeholders)
patterns.name: Default palette variants fail contrast (btn-warning, btn-info, alerts, placeholder)
patterns.description: Bootstrap's stock color variants — notably .btn-warning, .btn-info, .btn-success (dark text or white text on light fills) and muted placeholder text — produce text and UI-component contrast below 4.5:1 / 3:1 against light backgrounds. Sites that adopt the defaults unmodified inherit the failures across every page.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
<button class="btn btn-warning">Continue</button>
<!-- #ffc107 fill with near-black text region edges; white-text variants ~2-3:1 -->
<input class="form-control" placeholder="Search...">
<!-- placeholder ~ #6c757d on white -->
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one IS reliably automatable — axe/Lighthouse compute text contrast ratios and flag failing button/placeholder colors. Flagged false because a contrast checker catches it; the only caveat is large-text thresholds and overlay images, which can need human review.
patterns.realWorldNote: Bootstrap's own accessibility page admits default palette combinations may fall below WCAG contrast; twbs/bootstrap issue #25126 tracks failing AA combinations. https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/25126

patterns.platform: Shopify product pages, WooCommerce variation swatches, custom theme color/size pickers
patterns.name: Color-only variant swatches with no text label
patterns.description: Product variants are presented as colored squares/circles with no visible or programmatic text. The accessible name is empty or just a hex/SKU, and the selected state is shown only by a border or color change. Screen-reader and colorblind users cannot tell which color is which, nor which is currently selected.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: An empty-name swatch built as a div may trip a name check, but the deeper failures — that COLOR is the only means of conveying the option (1.4.1) and that the SELECTED state is communicated by visual styling alone — require a human to perceive the colors and reason that meaning is lost without them. No linter knows 'navy vs maroon' is the information.
patterns.realWorldNote: Shopify's own accessibility best-practices doc warns custom swatches commonly lose keyboard access and text labels: https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/best-practices/accessibility . EAA-driven swatch fixes: https://craftshift.com/shopify-european-accessibility-act-swatches/
